verses.commentary: Whenever I would heal Israel, Ephraim's sins are exposed. God's healing intention reveals the disease. Samaria's crimes revealed. Deceit practiced, thieves breaking in, bandits robbing. Sin cannot be hidden from the healer.
They do not realize I remember all their evil deeds. They forget that God remembers. Their sins engulf them. Surrounded by consequences. They are always before me. God's constant awareness.
They delight the king with their wickedness. Corruption as entertainment. Princes amused by lies. The court celebrates what God condemns.

They are all adulterers. Universal corruption. Burning like an oven. Internal fire of lust and conspiracy. The baker need not stir from kneading to rising. The heat sustains itself. Self-perpetuating sin.
On the day of our king's festival. Royal celebration. Princes inflamed with wine. Alcohol fuels conspiracy. He joins hands with mockers. The king himself participates in scorn.
Hearts like an oven. The heat metaphor continues. Passion smolders all night. In the morning it blazes. Conspiracy that waits for the right moment.

All of them hot as an oven. They devour their rulers. Internal political violence. All their kings fall. Rapid succession of assassinations. None of them calls on me. Through all the chaos, no turn to God.
Ephraim mixes with the nations. Loss of distinctiveness. A flat loaf not turned over. Half-baked, burnt on one side, raw on the other. Incomplete, ruined, useless.
Foreigners sap his strength. Gradual weakening. But he does not realize it. Oblivious decline. His hair is sprinkled with gray. Signs of aging unnoticed. They cannot see their own decay.
Israel's arrogance testifies against him. Pride as witness. Despite all this he does not return to the Lord. The refusal continues. Or search for him. Not even seeking.
Ephraim is like a dove. Easily deceived and senseless. Calling to Egypt, turning to Assyria. Flitting between superpowers. No consistent direction.
When they go, I will throw my net over them. God as hunter. I will pull them down like birds. The dove caught. Caught when they flock together. Their gathering becomes their capture.
Woe to them because they have strayed. Destruction because of rebellion. I long to redeem them. God's desire stated. But they speak lies about me. Their words about God are false.

They do not cry out to me from their hearts. Surface religion. They wail on their beds. Self-pity, not repentance. They slash themselves for grain and wine. Pagan ritual. But they turn away from me. The fundamental direction is wrong.
I trained them and strengthened their arms. God's past investment. But they plot evil against me. The trained turn on the trainer. Ingratitude as policy.

They do not turn to the Most High. Refusal to look up. They are like a faulty bow. Unreliable, missing the target. Leaders fall by the sword. Political violence. For their insolent words they will be ridiculed in Egypt. The nation they trusted will mock them.
